reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a list-style discussion of business and investment approaches, including crypto, crowdfunding, lending, property, and investment themes. The examples describe possible returns with time, business-performance, or risk conditions and explicitly instruct viewers to assess project risk. Shop-setup guidance and a premium-course link are described as ordinary commercial or channel promotion, without a stated deceptive promise or outcome.

citations.quote: 15 Easiest Ways to Make Money in 2022 (If You Already Have Some)
For those of you who have some money already lined up, by the end of this video you'll probably identify your next investment or at least get the confirmation that you're making the right call.
By far the easiest way to make money this decade is to simply buy some bitcoin or ethereum and literally do nothing else but hold it for the next 5-10 years.
Basically, you and other people come together and invest in early-stage companies.
In return, you own a percentage of that company if in a couple of years that company becomes highly profitable or gets acquired you make bank

opening.argument: Judge, this is more than a discussion of crypto as a market. The speaker calls buying bitcoin or ethereum and holding it for five to ten years “the easiest way to make money this decade.” That pairs a specific purchase and holding action with an unusually easy-money claim. The absence of a link to a seller does not erase the solicitation: viewers are told what to buy, what to do with it, and why they should expect to make money.

citations.quote: By far the easiest way to make money this decade is to simply buy some bitcoin or ethereum and literally do nothing else but hold it for the next 5-10 years.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls this conditional investment commentary, but its own crypto quotation contains no condition about price or performance. “Simply buy” and “literally do nothing else” are the operative instructions. Other examples in the list may describe risk or business performance; those qualifications do not change how directly this recommendation links a token purchase to easy money.

citations.quote: By far the easiest way to make money this decade is to simply buy some bitcoin or ethereum and literally do nothing else but hold it for the next 5-10 years.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted sentence recommends a long holding period, but it does not promise a fixed return, identify a seller, or send viewers into a token-purchase flow. The wider discussion distinguishes safer long-term investing from speculation, explicitly describing leverage trading as an option for someone willing to “risk it all.” An overconfident investment opinion is not, by itself, evidence of a deceptive scheme.

citations.quote: If you're feeling like you'd rather risk it all than play it safe, then look into leverage trading.
Have a lot? Go with an index fund and play it safe. The S&P 500 is probably your best bet to make money sustainably and long-term.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the cluster of easy-income signals. The speaker says online ads can return up to 30-50 times the spend, then directs viewers to a shop-setup destination that could have them operating by the end of the day with two weeks of premium services. The conditional phrase “if you know what you're doing” does little to substantiate that extraordinary return. The combination of a striking earnings figure, a near-immediate setup claim, and a destination for taking action warrants more scrutiny than a generic list of business ideas.

citations.quote: Online ads are crazy returns. If you know what you're doing you can get up to 30-50X returns on your spend.

If you go to alux.com slash sell, by the end of today you could have a full online shop setup, and you're going to get access for two weeks of premium services because Shopify wants to support our community.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense describes the shop link as ordinary promotion, but the link is presented immediately after a claim of up to 30-50X ad returns. Its reference to risk assessment concerns funded lending projects, not the advertised shop-and-ads sequence. Nor does saying campaigns may require tests establish that the highlighted return is representative.

citations.quote: It might require a few tests to figure out which campaign gets you the best results, but once you do you just keep those orders coming.
But make sure you look into the project you're funding and assess them based on the level of risk you're willing to take.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The 30-50X figure is expressly conditional, not a guaranteed result. The setup offer concerns an online shop and a limited period of premium services; the speaker then describes choosing a product, setting up payments, and testing campaigns. Those are ordinary steps in selling a product, and the cited material does not establish that the shop offer or return claim is deceptive.

citations.quote: If you know what you're doing you can get up to 30-50X returns on your spend.
Put your product onto Shopify. You set up a payment system with Paypal or Stripe and then begin to promote your high-margin product on the socials.
It might require a few tests to figure out which campaign gets you the best results

opening.argument: Judge, the list format should not obscure the video’s commercial direction. It invites viewers to identify a next investment, while the description points them to premium courses. Within the list, the speaker promotes a specific shop-setup destination and says viewers could have a shop by the end of the day, with temporary premium access. The finance-education framing thus also serves to move an audience seeking ways to make money toward the channel’s paid-service ecosystem. That promotional role matters when weighing its easy-income framing.

citations.quote: by the end of this video you'll probably identify your next investment or at least get the confirmation that you're making the right call.
Have a look at our premium courses: https://courses.alux.com

If you go to alux.com slash sell, by the end of today you could have a full online shop setup, and you're going to get access for two weeks of premium services because Shopify wants to support our community.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that a course link alone is ordinary promotion. The concern is its placement alongside an invitation to find a next investment and an actionable shop offer. Calling those elements “commercial promotion” describes their form, but does not answer whether the surrounding easy-money pitch is being used to draw viewers into them.

citations.quote: by the end of this video you'll probably identify your next investment or at least get the confirmation that you're making the right call.
Have a look at our premium courses: https://courses.alux.com

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A promotional element does not establish a scam. The description discloses the course link openly, and the shop segment identifies what viewers would do: put a product on Shopify, arrange payments, and promote it. The video also advises viewers with less than $5,000 saved to invest in their education rather than an outside investment. The cited material does not show a deceptive promise or concealed destination.

citations.quote: Have a look at our premium courses: https://courses.alux.com
Put your product onto Shopify. You set up a payment system with Paypal or Stripe and then begin to promote your high-margin product on the socials.
if you've got less than $5,000 saved up, that's not outside investment money!
